entries.originalText: “My Son, I the Lord am a stronghold in the day of trouble.(1) Come unto Me, when it is not well with thee.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son, I the Lord am a stronghold in the day of trouble.(1) Come to Me when it is not well with you.

entries.originalText: “This it is which chiefly hindereth heavenly consolation, that thou too slowly betakest thyself unto prayer.
entries.modernizedText: “This is what chiefly hinders heavenly consolation, that you turn to prayer too slowly.

entries.originalText: For before thou earnestly seekest unto Me, thou dost first seek after many means of comfort, and refresheth thyself in outward things: so it cometh to pass that all things profit thee but little until thou learn that it is I who deliver those who trust in Me; neither beside Me is there any strong help, nor profitable counsel, nor enduring remedy.
entries.modernizedText: For before you earnestly seek Me, you first seek after many means of comfort, and refresh yourself in outward things: so it comes to pass that all things profit you but little until you learn that it is I who deliver those who trust in Me; neither beside Me is there any strong help, or profitable counsel, or enduring remedy.

entries.originalText: But now, recovering courage after the tempest, grow thou strong in the light of My mercies, for I am nigh, saith the Lord, that I may restore all things not only as they were at the first, but also abundantly and one upon another.
entries.modernizedText: But now, recovering courage after the tempest, grow strong in the light of My mercies, for I am near, says the Lord, that I may restore all things not only as they were at first, but also abundantly and one upon another.

entries.originalText: “For is anything too hard for Me, or shall I be like unto one who saith and doeth not?
entries.modernizedText: “For is anything too hard for Me, or shall I be like one who says and does not do?

entries.originalText: Where is thy faith?
entries.modernizedText: Where is your faith?

entries.originalText: Stand fast and with perseverance.
entries.modernizedText: Stand fast and with perseverance.

entries.originalText: Be long-suffering and strong.
entries.modernizedText: Be long-suffering and strong.

entries.originalText: Consolation will come unto thee in its due season.
entries.modernizedText: Consolation will come to you in its due season.

entries.originalText: Wait for Me; yea, wait; I will come and heal thee.
entries.modernizedText: Wait for Me; yes, wait; I will come and heal you.

entries.originalText: It is temptation which vexeth thee, and a vain fear which terrifieth thee.
entries.modernizedText: It is temptation which vexes you, and a vain fear which terrifies you.

entries.originalText: What doth care about future events bring thee, save sorrow upon sorrow?
entries.modernizedText: What does care about future events bring you, except sorrow upon sorrow?

entries.originalText: Sufficient for the day is the evil thereof.(2) It is vain and useless to be disturbed or lifted up about future things which perhaps will never come.
entries.modernizedText: Sufficient for the day is its evil.(2) It is vain and useless to be disturbed or lifted up about future things which perhaps will never come.

entries.originalText: “But it is the nature of man to be deceived by fancies of this sort, and it is a sign of a mind which is still weak to be so easily drawn away at the suggestion of the enemy.
entries.modernizedText: “But it is the nature of man to be deceived by fancies of this sort, and it is a sign of a mind which is still weak to be so easily drawn away at the suggestion of the enemy.

entries.originalText: For he careth not whether he deceive and beguile by true means or false; whether he throw thee down by the love of the present or fear of the future.
entries.modernizedText: For he does not care whether he deceives and beguiles by true means or false; whether he throws you down by the love of the present or fear of the future.

entries.originalText: Therefore let not thy heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore do not let your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

entries.originalText: Believe in Me, and put thy trust in My mercy.(3) When thou thinkest thyself far removed from Me, I am often the nearer.
entries.modernizedText: Believe in Me, and put your trust in My mercy.(3) When you think yourself far removed from Me, I am often nearer.

entries.originalText: When thou reckonest that almost all is lost, then often is greater opportunity of gain at hand.
entries.modernizedText: When you reckon that almost all is lost, then often a greater opportunity of gain is at hand.

entries.originalText: All is not lost when something goeth contrary to thy wishes.
entries.modernizedText: All is not lost when something goes contrary to your wishes.

entries.originalText: Thou oughtest not to judge according to present feeling, nor so to take or give way to any grief which befalleth thee, as if all hope of escape were taken away.
entries.modernizedText: You ought not to judge according to present feeling, nor so take or give way to any grief which befalls you as if all hope of escape were taken away.

entries.originalText: “Think not thyself totally abandoned, although for the time I have sent to thee some tribulation, or have even withdrawn some cherished consolation; for this is the way to the Kingdom of Heaven.
entries.modernizedText: “Do not think yourself totally abandoned, although for the time I have sent you some tribulation, or have even withdrawn some cherished consolation; for this is the way to the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.originalText: And without doubt it is better for thee and for all My other servants, that ye should be proved by adversities, than that ye should have all things as ye would.
entries.modernizedText: And without doubt it is better for you and for all My other servants that you should be tested by adversities, than that you should have all things as you would.

entries.originalText: I know thy hidden thoughts: and that it is very needful for thy soul’s health that sometimes thou be left without relish, lest perchance thou be lifted up by prosperity, and desirous to please thyself in that which thou art not.
entries.modernizedText: I know your hidden thoughts: and that it is very needful for your soul’s health that sometimes you be left without relish, lest perhaps you be lifted up by prosperity, and desire to please yourself in that which you are not.

entries.originalText: What I have given I am able to take away, and to restore again at My good pleasure.
entries.modernizedText: What I have given I am able to take away, and to restore again at My good pleasure.

entries.originalText: “When I shall have given, it is Mine; when I shall have taken away, I have not taken what is thine; for every good gift and every perfect gift(4) is from me.
entries.modernizedText: “When I have given, it is Mine; when I have taken away, I have not taken what is yours; for every good gift and every perfect gift(4) is from Me.

entries.originalText: If I shall have sent upon thee grief or any vexation, be not angry, nor let thy heart be sad; I am able quickly to lift thee up and to change every burden into joy.
entries.modernizedText: If I have sent upon you grief or any vexation, do not be angry, or let your heart be sad; I am able quickly to lift you up and to change every burden into joy.

entries.originalText: But I am just and greatly to be praised, when I do thus unto thee.
entries.modernizedText: But I am just and greatly to be praised when I do thus to you.

entries.originalText: “If thou rightly consider, and look upon it with truth, thou oughtest never to be so sadly cast down because of adversity, but rather shouldst rejoice and give thanks; yea, verily to count it the highest joy that I afflict thee with sorrows and spare thee not.
entries.modernizedText: “If you rightly consider, and look upon it with truth, you ought never to be so sadly cast down because of adversity, but rather should rejoice and give thanks; indeed, truly count it the highest joy that I afflict you with sorrows and do not spare you.

entries.originalText: As My Father hath loved Me, so love I you;(5) thus have I spoken unto My beloved disciples: whom I sent forth not unto worldly joys, but to great strivings; not unto honours, but unto contempt; not unto ease, but to labours; not unto rest, but to bring forth much fruit with patience.
entries.modernizedText: As My Father has loved Me, so I love you;(5) thus I have spoken to My beloved disciples: whom I sent forth not to worldly joys, but to great strivings; not to honors, but to contempt; not to ease, but to labors; not to rest, but to bring forth much fruit with patience.

entries.originalText: My son, remember these words.”
entries.modernizedText: My son, remember these words.”
